Phase: web app surface discovery structure-aware extension
Business goal: Refresh both discovered leaf truth and discovered structure truth so later hierarchy reconcile can consume an honest discovered tree instead of inferring structure from flat paths.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can trigger discovery and persist current discovered surfaces plus the current discovered structure tree for approved root families.
Notes / constraints: Must preserve the existing truth-layer split: discovered surfaces remain canonical leaf truth, discovered structure nodes remain canonical discovered grouping truth, and curated hierarchy remains separate. The capability must not invent curated pages or silently flatten group nodes into page nodes. The existing explicit root-triggered sync posture still applies.
Tenant context rule: root-operated capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may run structure-aware discovery.
Authz scope type: root-scoped sync over approved discovery scope
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in this loop because the extension remains backend and persistence focused.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before discovery. The feature must orchestrate approved providers, normalize both discovered surfaces and discovered structure nodes, upsert current rows, write per-run observation history, mark stale rows safely, and reject malformed structure graphs such as duplicate sibling keys or invalid parent-child posture.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: No client-side behavior in this loop.
Request contract: Body remains an explicit approved discovery scope. Clients cannot submit invented structure trees or discovered surfaces directly.
Response contract: Returns discovery-run summary that now includes structure-aware counts or summaries sufficient to understand both leaf and structure refresh posture.
Error contract: 400 invalid scope or provider output; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 409 malformed structure graph or incompatible provider output; 500 only for unexpected infrastructure failure.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes approved frontend provider seams and later feeds discovered tree reads into `webAppHierarchyBuilder` reconcile capabilities.
Persistence impact: Adds durable current discovered-structure rows plus per-run discovered-structure observations alongside the existing surface and run tables.
Indexes / uniqueness: Unique index on structure node identity key. Parent-child traversal indexes. Existing discovered-surface uniqueness still applies. Additional indexes on rootFamilyId nodeKind staleAt and lastDiscoveredAt support tree reads and stale review.
Search / filter model: Explicit structure-tree reads and exact reads by stable ids. Avoid vague search blobs in the first structure-aware slice.
Compatibility / migration notes: Backwards compatibility is required by default. The extension must not reinterpret existing leaf truth ambiguously
Authentication requirement: must not hard-delete current rows during normal refresh
Authorization enforcement layer: and must not collapse group structure into curated hierarchy automatically.
Audit requirement: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local provider and structure validation.
Privacy / personal data impact: No direct browser impact in API-only slice.
Standards impact: Audit successful runs and denied attempts with actor rootUserId scope summary provider results surface counts structure counts and blocking failure summaries.
PRD required?: Low to moderate; persists internal app-structure metadata only.
ADR required?: ASVS authorization and anti-drift relevance remain high because this becomes the durable discovered tree source for later reconcile work.
column66: Capability is acceptable when a privileged operator can refresh honest discovered surface truth plus honest discovered structure truth without inventing curated hierarchy or flattening grouping nodes into fake pages.

Phase: web app surface discovery structure-aware extension
Business goal: Expose the current discovered structure tree so operators and downstream reconcile flows can inspect real implemented app grouping and nesting.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can retrieve the current discovered tree for a root family and see grouping nodes, leaf nodes, linked discovered surfaces, and stale posture explicitly.
Notes / constraints: Reads must not pretend discovered groups are curated pages. The tree should remain discovery-owned truth, preserve node kinds, preserve parent-child posture, and preserve links to leaf discovered surfaces where applicable.
Tenant context rule: root-operated capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may read discovered structure truth.
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in this loop because the extension remains backend and persistence focused.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before structure-tree reads. The feature must return explicit node kinds parent-child structure linked discovered surface ids when present provider posture and stale posture without leaking private provider internals that are outside the contract.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: No client-side behavior in this loop.
Request contract: List query should at minimum support rootFamilyId staleStatus includeSupportOnly includeReviewRequired page/pageSize only where a flat exact-node catalog is also exposed. Tree read may use rootFamilyId plus explicit posture filters.
Response contract: Returns a tree or exact-node payload with stable structure-node ids parent ids nodeKind segmentKey displayLabel depth linkedDiscoveredWebAppSurfaceId providerKey implementationSourcePath firstDiscoveredAt lastDiscoveredAt staleAt and child nodes when tree mode is requested.
Error contract: 400 invalid query or identifier; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 exact node not found.
Cross-feature seams: Later hierarchy preview and apply or sync capabilities should consume these structure reads instead of inferring tree shape from path strings.
Persistence impact: Read-only access to current discovered structure truth and linked leaf metadata. No mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Indexes on rootFamilyId parentNodeId nodeKind staleAt and lastDiscoveredAt support tree traversal and filtering. Exact-node lookups require stable primary key and unique structure identity key.
Search / filter model: Tree traversal and exact reads by explicit fields only. No broad fuzzy search is required in the first structure-aware slice.
Compatibility / migration notes: Default reads should stay compatible with later structure-aware reconcile consumers by preserving explicit node kinds and links rather than flattening group nodes into strings only.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local exact and filtered read validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only slice.
Audit requirement: Audit denied structure-tree reads if visibility remains privileged; successful reads are optional.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; exposes internal app-structure metadata only to privileged root operators.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization relevance and strong anti-drift value because these reads become the safe discovered-tree seam for later hierarchy reconcile logic.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged operator can inspect the current discovered tree with explicit group and leaf nodes, linked leaf-surface truth, and no confusion between discovered structure and curated hierarchy.

Phase: web app hierarchy structure-aware reconcile extension
Business goal: Show how the discovered structure tree would map into curated hierarchy truth before any hierarchy mutation happens.
User outcome: A privileged root operator can review how discovered groups and leaves might map into curated modules, pages, or blocked outcomes before applying a reconcile step.
Notes / constraints: Preview must not mutate discovered truth or curated hierarchy truth. It must preserve which discovered nodes are groups, which are leaves, which links already exist, and which nodes are blocked because the curated hierarchy model still lacks an approved mapping rule.
Tenant context rule: root-operated capability outside tenant-scoped authorization; no tenant context applies
Explicitly denied roles: tenant actors; unauthenticated callers; authenticated root users without the governing capability
Authorization summary: Only privileged root operators may preview structure-aware reconcile.
Authz scope type: root-scoped preview over discovered structure scope and hierarchy scope
Frontend visibility rule: No frontend surface is required in this first structure-aware loop because the extension remains backend focused.
Backend enforcement rule: Root auth and root authorization must run before preview. The feature must consume public discovered structure reads, compare them to curated hierarchy truth and future discovery-link bridge records, and return planned mappings or blocking reasons without mutating persistence.
Session / expiry behavior: Uses existing authenticated root-session expiry rules. No tenant session behavior applies.
Client-side permission behavior: No client-side behavior in this loop.
Request contract: Body identifies selected discovered root families, structure-node ids, or whole-tree scopes plus optional hierarchy scope and mapping strategy posture.
Response contract: Returns preview summary with proposed module mappings page mappings blocked nodes support-only skips shell-state blocks unmatched nodes and conflict reasons plus per-node planned action detail.
Error contract: 400 invalid preview scope; 401 unauthenticated; 403 unauthorized; 404 referenced discovery or hierarchy records not found; 409 preview blocked by incompatible hierarchy state or missing approved mapping rule.
Cross-feature seams: Consumes public discovered structure reads from `webAppSurfaceDiscovery` plus curated hierarchy reads and future discovery-link rows.
Persistence impact: Read-only compare across discovered structure truth discovered surface truth curated hierarchy truth and future bridge records. No mutation.
Indexes / uniqueness: Future bridge indexes on discovered structure node ids discovered surface ids curated module ids and curated page ids will matter once the link model exists.
Search / filter model: Preview by explicit tree scope or exact node ids only. Avoid broad fuzzy search in the first structure-aware reconcile slice.
Compatibility / migration notes: Preview is the safe compatibility boundary before structure-aware import. It must not silently invent curated hierarchy from discovered grouping nodes without explicit mapping rules.
Authorization enforcement layer: Root auth middleware plus root authorization enforcement and feature-local reconcile preview validation.
CSP / browser security impact: No direct browser impact in API-only slice.
Audit requirement: Audit successful previews and denied attempts if reconcile visibility is treated as privileged.
Privacy / personal data impact: Low; preview exposes internal app-structure and hierarchy metadata only to privileged root operators.
Standards impact: ASVS authorization and anti-drift relevance are high because preview protects the separation between discovered tree truth and curated hierarchy truth.
Acceptance notes: Capability is acceptable when a privileged operator can review an honest no-mutation structure-aware preview that shows groups leaves links blocks and conflicts explicitly.
